source_name: ECB SPACE — Study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (hub)
why_relevant: The definitive cash-usage-at-POS evidence base, run since 2016 (2016/2019/2022/2024 waves) with country-level results. Slovenia is repeatedly among the highest cash-share countries (64% of POS payments by number in 2024), which is decisive context for cash-handling, ATM and POS strategy. No national equivalent exists.

source_name: ECB SPACE 2024 statistical annexes (Annex A/B country tables)
why_relevant: Country-by-country breakdowns (payment shares by instrument, value bands, P2P, online, cash access/acceptance perceptions) where the Slovenia column lives. This is the extractable layer, not the narrative report.

source_name: ECB — Use of cash by companies in the euro area (SUCH / company cash survey)
why_relevant: Merchant/company-side counterpart to SPACE (waves 2021, 2024, 2026): cash acceptance rates, deposit/withdrawal behaviour, payment-method acceptance criteria. Directly relevant to POS acceptance and cash-handling demand in Slovenia; euro-area cash acceptance fell 96%->88% between 2021 and 2024.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — Banknotes statistics (BKN)
why_relevant: Monthly national-issuance (net) series of euro banknotes and coins per NCB, plus semi-annual cash-logistics data — an objective, high-frequency proxy for cash demand in Slovenia to triangulate with SPACE survey cash shares.

source_name: ECB — Payments statistics indicators (key figures dashboard)
why_relevant: Curated headline indicator set (per-capita card payments, terminal counts, instrument mix) that is quickest for cross-country benchmarking of Slovenia without building SDMX keys.

source_name: ECB — Payments statistics methodology / data-category notes
why_relevant: Defines concepts, reporting population, frequency (semi-annual, with quarterly high-level and card indicators) and publication lag (H1 by end-Jan, H2 by end-Jul). Needed to avoid mis-comparing SI figures across regimes and to time collection.

source_name: EBA–ECB Joint Report on Payment Fraud (annual series)
why_relevant: Annual EU/EEA fraud dataset under PSD2 with country-level breakdowns by instrument (cards, credit transfers, direct debits, cash withdrawals, e-money) and SCA vs non-SCA splits. Gives Slovenia a comparative fraud-risk position; 2024 EEA card losses EUR 1.329bn (+29% YoY).

source_name: EBA Payment Institutions Register (PIR, PSD2 central register)
why_relevant: Authoritative EU-wide register of authorised payment institutions, e-money institutions, PISPs, AISPs and their agents, filterable by country of establishment — the cleanest way to enumerate and track the Slovenian non-bank PSP population over time. Whole register is downloadable.

source_name: EBA Credit Institutions Register (CIR) and other lists of institutions (EUCLID)
why_relevant: Master data on credit institutions and other supervised entities across the EU, sourced from EUCLID; gives the authoritative, comparable list of Slovenian banks/branches underlying any market-structure or bank-count analysis.

source_name: European Commission (DG FISMA) — Payment services policy hub
why_relevant: Central pointer to PSD2/PSD3-PSR, Instant Payments Regulation, digital euro legislative files, impact assessments and consultation responses — the regulatory drivers that reshape the Slovenian payments market and often carry country-level annexes/studies.

source_name: European Court of Auditors — Special Report 01/2025 'Digital payments in the EU'
why_relevant: Independent audit of EU digital-payments policy; audits typically expose data gaps, supervisory weaknesses and member-state comparisons that are not visible in ECB statistics, and cite underlying datasets useful for snowballing.

source_name: ECB Euro Retail Payments Board (ERPB) — statements and instant-payments reporting
why_relevant: ERPB statements track SCT Inst reachability/adoption and market-side deliverables; a leading indicator of instant-payment rollout affecting Slovenian banks ahead of statistical confirmation in PSS.

source_name: ECB Retail Payments Strategy hub
why_relevant: Frames ECB's own priorities (pan-European solutions, digital euro, instant payments) and links to the reports and oversight frameworks that determine what statistics get published next.

source_name: Eurostat — ICT usage / e-banking and e-commerce datasets (isoc_bde15cbc, isoc_i, isoc_e)
why_relevant: EU-harmonised household/enterprise survey data on internet banking, online purchasing and enterprise web sales with Slovenia as a country row; the standard demand-side complement to ECB payment counts (e.g. SI web-sales share of turnover 4.63%).

source_name: Banka Slovenije coverage of ECB studies (Slovenian-language gateway to SPACE)
source_subtype: NCB press release relaying supranational study
why_relevant: The NCB's Slovenian-language write-up of the ECB SPACE results is the only place euro-area cash-study findings are rendered with explicit Slovenian framing and local terminology; it is also the practical entry point for sl-language discovery of ECB material (ECB itself publishes SPACE/PSS almost exclusively in English).

source_name: Banka Slovenije — payment statistics reporting instructions (Poročanje podatkov statistike plačil)
source_subtype: reporting/methodology page (national leg of EU dataset)
why_relevant: Documents the national implementation of ECB Regulation ECB/2020/59 — which SI institutions report, on what templates and deadlines. Explains the provenance, granularity and lag of the SI rows that appear in ECB PSS/PTT, and names reporting-agent categories for actor mapping.

source_name: OPSI – Podatki o davčno potrjenih računih (FURS fiscal-verification open data)
why_relevant: Daily open dataset of the number and value of ALL fiscally verified invoices in Slovenia, broken to 5-digit SKD activity level. Because ZDavPR defines 'cash payment' broadly (banknotes/coins PLUS card and any non-direct-transfer settlement), this is the single largest merchant-side proxy for till-level transaction volume and value per retail sector — the denominator against which card/POS transaction counts can be benchmarked.

source_name: FURS – Davčne blagajne in vezane knjige računov (fiscal verification programme pages)
why_relevant: The regulator's own programme area for davčno potrjevanje računov: legal definition of 'plačilo z gotovino' (which crucially includes card payments), obligations of merchants, supervision statistics and penalty reporting. Needed to correctly interpret any fiscal data and to understand what POS/ECR vendors must implement in Slovenia.

source_name: eDavki / FURS – Davčno potrjevanje računov: tehnične specifikacije
why_relevant: Technical spec (XML schemas, message fields, digital certificate rules) that every Slovenian ECR/POS software vendor must implement. Reveals exactly which fields — including payment-related ones — are transmitted per invoice, which bounds what fiscal data can ever show about card vs cash, and is a hard integration requirement for any POS/terminal vendor entering SI.

source_name: Mercator Group – Annual reports / investor relations
why_relevant: Slovenia's largest grocery retailer by store count (~740 stores, ~30% share). Annual reports document store network size, checkout/self-checkout ('Tik-Tak' hitre blagajne) rollout, the Pika loyalty/payment card scheme and M Pay wallet — i.e. the acceptance footprint and own-scheme payment instruments of the biggest single POS estate in the country.

source_name: SEOnet (Ljubljanska borza) – issuer disclosures incl. Mercator
why_relevant: Regulated-information hub where Mercator and other listed SI issuers file annual/interim reports and corporate governance documents. Acts as a stable, machine-navigable pointer to retailer financials even when corporate sites reorganise; also surfaces bond prospectuses that describe the retail network in detail.

source_name: Petrol Group – Annual report and investor disclosures
why_relevant: Petrol operates the densest unattended/attended retail payment network in SI (fuel stations, EV charging). Its reports cover the Petrol klub loyalty card and its successor 'Petrol Pay' payment card, plus retail transaction volumes — a rare case of a Slovenian merchant issuing its own payment instrument. Petrol has been publicly cited as roughly 50/50 cash vs card at the till.

source_name: AJPES – JOLP public annual reports of retail companies (SPAR, Hofer, Lidl, Tuš, Jager)
why_relevant: Foreign-owned SI grocers (SPAR Slovenija ~EUR 1.16bn, Hofer ~EUR 674m, Lidl ~EUR 639m) are not listed and disclose only via AJPES statutory filings. This is the authoritative way to size the merchant-side transaction pool per chain and to track store-count and revenue growth that drives terminal and self-checkout demand.

source_name: Bizi.si – company financial profiles and retail-sector rankings
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator of AJPES data that publishes ready-made 'largest Slovenian retailers' comparisons; far cheaper to monitor than filing-by-filing AJPES work, and its editorial pieces are a reliable annual pointer to who the top merchant counterparties are.

source_name: SURS / OPSI – Trgovina na drobno (retail trade turnover statistics)
why_relevant: Official retail-trade turnover by broad merchandise group and by main activity — the macro denominator for merchant-side payments analysis. Combined with the FURS fiscal series it lets you separate 'total retail spend' from 'spend that passes through a fiscally verified till'.

source_name: GZS – Trgovinska zbornica Slovenije (Chamber of Commerce, trade section): current trade statistics
why_relevant: The merchants' own trade association: publishes curated current trade statistics, sector position papers and is the counterparty in policy debates on cash acceptance obligations and interchange/terminal costs. A prime pointer to merchant sentiment and to further merchant-side data.

source_name: Mikropis Holding / MikroPOS – Slovenian ECR and self-checkout vendor
why_relevant: The domestic incumbent in Slovenian retail checkout: installed the first self-checkouts in SI (Mercator 'Tik-Tak', 2007) and exports to China and South Korea (E-Mart). Its product and reference pages are the closest thing to a public inventory of self-checkout and ECR deployments in Slovenian retail — direct evidence of till-level automation and of the competitive landscape any POS/terminal vendor faces.
